Can Redwood run sizing recs (recommended GPU count + buffer) and a target SLA we can sign to? Also include timeline to provision so we can sync with infra changes on our side.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — procurement will want an updated quote and T&Cs.

Thanks,

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Fwd: Dedicated pool upsizing before renewal — sizing + commercial needed

Hi team — reviewed the CSV and ran sizing sims against the model family AlphaSoft runs (redwood/gpt-large-llm-1 and a quantized 4-bit variant). Key points below; full workbook attached in the proposal PDF.

Assumptions (baseline):
- Peak sustained QPS observed: 380 (observed 2-hr window).
- Avg tokens per call: 240
- Typical request target latency SLO: 300–500ms p95
- Running gpt-large-llm-1 (fp16) performance: ~9k tokens/sec per A100-80GB equiv under our batching profile. Quantized 4-bit path: ~6k tokens/sec per GPU but ~1.5x more conservative on latency tail for long contexts.

Sizing calc (target: cover 95th percentile bursts with 20% headroom):
- Tokens/sec at 380 QPS * 240 tokens = 91,200 tokens/sec sustained during peak
- Add 20% headroom => 109,440 tokens/sec required
- FP16 A100-equivalent GPUs needed = 109,440 / 9,000 ≈ 12.16 => recommend 13 GPUs (A100-equivalent)
- Quantized 4-bit variant recommended option = 109,440 / 6,000 ≈ 18.24 => recommend 19 GPUs (for same headroom; cheaper per-GPU running cost assumed)

Operational recommendations:
- Reserved pool: provision 13 x A100-equivalent GPUs as primary configuration, with an option to convert 6 of those to quantized instances after a two-week quality validation to reduce cost if latency/accuracy meet their evals.
- Autoscale burst: add 4 on-demand GPUs (no reserve) for extreme events (can be charged at on-demand rate).
- Network/throughput: shard requests across 3 inference nodes to keep KV cache warm; recommend rolling canary over 48 hours.
- SLA suggestion: 99.5% availability for reserved pool plus a documented fallback to a slightly cheaper quantized model family in case of capacity constraints.

Attachments: "redwood_reserved_pool_proposal_v2.pdf" (contains pricing ranges, provisioning schedule, and quality impact notes).

Happy to walk through numbers on a quick call.

- Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>

Emma — thanks for the data and Marissa for the sizing. Quick commercial note:

Timeline: if they sign by 2026-11-01 we can provision the reserved pool and start a staged rollout the week of 2026-11-08. DocuSign link will be provided with the revised quote + SOW.

Thanks,
Connor O'Brien
